question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s entrenched control over the Chinese Communist Party, reinforced by extensive purges of military and civilian officials and the elevation of loyalists such as Cai Qi, underpins trader expectations that he will remain in power through 2026. With no term limits in place and preparations underway for a fourth term at the 21st Party Congress in late 2027, recent developments including anti-corruption drives, personnel reshuffles favoring personal networks, and public emphasis on party discipline and national security priorities show no erosion of his authority. Succession questions remain deferred, with no designated heir or signs of elite contestation emerging. While abrupt health developments or an unprecedented internal challenge could theoretically alter this trajectory before the end of 2026, current evidence of centralized decision-making and institutional dominance sustains the strong market consensus reflected in these odds.
